note: The skill table (plan.md 4.5.2.2), on branch calculator-runner since 2026-11-11. skills[] holds one manifest per landed skill version, in the meta-agent repository's skill.schema.json field names with three differences this file's schema states. planned[] holds drafts in the same shape whose code and running case have not landed; a draft is in no floor. legacy_inequalities[] lists what the axis modules still compute themselves. rows[] holds, per observable and configuration, the legacy inequalities a question leaves out, each with its reason and the person's confirming words. The floor for a question is every skill in skills[] whose applies_to matches, plus every legacy inequality of that agent that no confirmed exclusion removes. All of it runs, the model may add a landed skill with a reason, and nothing is dropped.
default_not_applied_reason: Nothing in contracts/skills.json applies this to the question's observable and configuration, so it was not run. It says nothing about whether it would bind.

planned.summary: The drag coefficient expected for a sphere moving parallel to one plane wall, at a given height of its centre.

inputs.name: viscosity
inputs.meaning: viscosity of the medium at the sample temperature

inputs.name: bead_centre_height
inputs.meaning: distance from the bead's centre to the wall

outputs.name: drag_coefficient
outputs.meaning: bulk Stokes drag times the parallel wall correction

source.citation: Tolić-Nørrelykke, Schäffer, Howard, Pavone, Jülicher & Flyvbjerg, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 77, 103101 (2006)
source.locus: Eq. 39 for the bulk drag and Eq. 40 for the parallel wall correction, a series in radius over centre height

planned.validity: one plane no-slip wall, low Reynolds number, and a centre height above the ratio the source states for the series

planned.summary: The lowest bead-centre height at which the parallel wall correction's series is as accurate as its source states.

inputs.name: wall_series_validity_ratio
inputs.meaning: the centre-height-to-radius ratio above which the source states the series is accurate, taken from the source's entry and never written into the code

source.citation: Tolić-Nørrelykke, Schäffer, Howard, Pavone, Jülicher & Flyvbjerg, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 77, 103101 (2006)
source.locus: Appendix D: where the series of Eq. 40 agrees with the exact result, and to what accuracy

planned.summary: The highest bead-centre height at which the wall still changes the drag by more than the target relative error.

inputs.name: drag_relative_error
inputs.meaning: the question's target relative error on the drag, from the goal: a judgement, bound to a row with its own source, and the person may replace it

outputs.name: bead_centre_height_max
outputs.meaning: the height at which the parallel wall correction equals the target relative error

source.citation: Tolić-Nørrelykke, Schäffer, Howard, Pavone, Jülicher & Flyvbjerg, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 77, 103101 (2006)
source.locus: Eq. 40, solved for the height at which the correction falls to the target

planned.validity: one plane no-slip wall; a second wall adds its own correction

planned.summary: The shortest record at one height from which the fitted diffusion coefficient, and so the drag, reaches the target relative error.

inputs.name: trap_stiffness
inputs.meaning: stiffness of the trap at the laser power used

inputs.name: drag_coefficient
inputs.meaning: the bead's drag at this height, the output of drag_parallel_to_wall

inputs.name: drag_relative_error
inputs.meaning: the question's target relative error on the drag, from the goal: a judgement, bound to a row with its own source, and the person may replace it

outputs.name: record_duration_min
outputs.meaning: the record length at which the fit's relative error equals the target

source.locus: the statistical error of the fitted corner frequency and diffusion coefficient against measurement time

planned.validity: a Lorentzian position power spectrum fitted over a range that contains the corner frequency

planned.summary: The longest exposure for which the variance lost to motion blur stays inside the range where the source's blur correction holds.

inputs.name: trap_stiffness
inputs.meaning: stiffness of the trap at the laser power used

inputs.name: drag_coefficient
inputs.meaning: the bead's drag at this height, the output of drag_parallel_to_wall

inputs.name: blur_correction_valid_ratio
inputs.meaning: the exposure-over-relaxation-time ratio up to which the source states its correction holds, taken from the source's entry and never written into the code

outputs.name: exposure_time_max
outputs.meaning: the ratio times the relaxation time, drag over stiffness

source.locus: Eq. 7, the factor by which a finite exposure lowers the measured variance, and the range of its stated approximation

planned.validity: an overdamped bead in a harmonic trap, tracked by a camera with a uniform exposure

planned.summary: The bead-centre height that a nominal focus travel from surface contact gives, through the objective's effective focal shift.

inputs.name: nominal_focus_travel
inputs.meaning: stage or objective travel from the position where the bead touches the surface

inputs.name: focal_shift_factor
inputs.meaning: bead displacement per unit of nominal travel for the objective in use, measured on this instrument; a paper's value for another objective is a reference and never this input

inputs.name: bead_radius
inputs.meaning: radius of the trapped bead, which is the centre height at contact

source.locus: the definition of the effective focal shift: the bead's axial displacement over the coverslip's

planned.validity: a trap whose axial position follows the focus linearly over the travel used
planned.note: When no measured factor exists for the objective, the run is refused before any code runs, and that refusal is how a plan learns the factor has to be measured first.

legacy_inequalities.statement: through the spinning disk, exposure = n * disk_period, or stripes remain
exposure long enough that the tracer's signal-to-noise reaches the target
the tracer has to clear the detection limit in a single frame, since a centroid is fitted per frame and not to a sum
background stays below the tracer signal by the margin the target needs
exposure short enough that a freely diffusing tracer does not smear across more than one pixel within a frame
the signal-to-noise holds for the whole record, not only at its start
the record spans enough diffusive times that a mean squared displacement has a slope to fit
each lag time carries enough independent displacements that the fitted slope reaches the target relative error
enough tracers are in the field at once to supply those displacements without extending the record
enough independent repeats to separate the sample's spread from the measurement's
the cumulative dose the sample receives stays below what damages it
the label surviving at the end of the record is enough that the observable is read from the sample rather than from its depletion
optical heating leaves the sample temperature inside the band the observable can tolerate
dense enough that a field carries trackable tracers, dilute enough that they neither interact nor overlap in the image
every device this configuration declares exists in the registry and has a control channel
the selector states this configuration needs form a tuple the optical-path table lists, so light actually reaches the detector
no two selectors this configuration must hold at once contend for one exclusive resource
every selector the plan must set can be set without a human, and any condition attached to that claim holds
every selector the plan must set can be confirmed to be in the state it was set to; an unverified state does not proceed (2.1)
focus must not wander further over the record than the measurement can tolerate: drift_rate * record_length <= focus_tolerance
focus stabilisation must be disabled across a turret or optical-path change and re-acquired after it, and no acquisition may span that bracket
nothing may be acquired while the spinning disk is still coming up to speed
a measurement may not start until the mechanics have settled after the turret, stage or path last moved
exposures, overheads and settling together must fit the time the session has
the run must fit a window in which the instrument is free, and moves that share a lock group cannot be scheduled to overlap
the diffraction-limited spot must be no larger than the smallest feature the observable needs resolved: k*lambda/NA <= required_lateral_resolution
the pixel projected into the sample must be at most half the diffraction-limited spot: pixel_size/magnification <= k*lambda/(2*NA)
the imaged area must cover what the question needs to see at once: sensor_active_area/magnification >= required_field_of_view
out-of-focus rejection must be enough that the observable is not contaminated by tracers outside the focal plane
the axial range that stays in focus must cover the tracer's axial excursion over the record: n*lambda/NA**2 >= axial_excursion
x_min*kappa/gamma <= v <= x_max*kappa/gamma: below the window the offset cannot be resolved, above it drag beats the trap and the bead leaves
f_s >= 10*f_c with f_c = kappa/(2*pi*gamma): sampling below ten times the corner frequency loses the trap's own response
x_min = sigma_loc/target_relative_error: the smallest offset worth commanding follows from the target, and is not chosen
t_settle = ln(1/target)*gamma/kappa: acquisition starts after the trap has settled, and this number is an input to A5 rather than a bound of its own
per-trap power ~ total/N, so per-trap stiffness falls with N; multiplexing adds a channel count and an update rate, and traps interfere below a minimum spacing
piezo range, bandwidth and settling, and the motorised stage's speed, acceleration, backlash and repeatability, bound commanded motion
total power meets P0's limit before it meets the sample's: whatever else this axis emits is a subset of the safety envelope

requires_legacy.why: Bead radius spread goes straight into the drag, so the number of beads measured per series is a requirement, not a convenience.
The trap laser heats the water around the bead, and the viscosity, hence the drag, falls with temperature. At the store's rough full-power figure this is several kelvin.
A second bead within tens of radii couples to the trapped one through the wall and changes its drag, so the sample must be dilute enough to isolate one bead.
Every configuration must be drivable; this question changes nothing about that.
Every configuration must put light where it is read; this question changes nothing about that.
Every configuration must avoid contended selectors; the tweezers hold a camera exclusively.
Every selector the plan sets must be settable without a person, or the plan says who sets it.
Every selector the plan sets must be confirmed; an unverified state does not proceed.
Axial drift during a record changes the bead's height, which is the controlled variable.
Focus stabilisation holds the objective-to-coverslip distance that every height is measured from.
Each height step moves the stage; a record taken before it settles mixes two heights.
A height series is many records; it has to fit the session.
The tweezers, camera and piezo are shared; the run needs a window where they are free.
The stage-oscillation check moves the fluid past the trapped bead; too fast and the bead leaves, too slow and the response is not resolved.
The drag comes from the position spectrum, which must be sampled above the trap's corner frequency to be fitted.
The localisation error sets the smallest response worth commanding, and it is the noise floor of the spectrum.
After each move the bead must re-equilibrate in the trap before a record starts.
Heights are set and the oscillation is driven by the piezo stage; its range, bandwidth and settling bound both.
Total optical power meets the safety limit before anything else; the runtime still enforces the limit at execution.

excluded.why: This row covers the transmitted configuration, which has no spinning disk in the path.
Bright-field tracking of a micrometre bead is not signal-limited; the localisation error that does limit it enters through resolvable_offset_floor.
A micrometre bead in bright field is far above any detection limit; the localisation error enters through resolvable_offset_floor.
There is no fluorescence background in transmitted bright field.
This bound is for a freely diffusing tracer; a trapped bead's blur is set by its relaxation time and is camera_blur_ceiling's.
Transmitted bright field excites no dye, so the signal does not decay over a record.
That bound is for a mean squared displacement; the drag here is read from a position power spectrum, whose record length is drag_record_length_floor's.
That bound is for a mean squared displacement fit; the drag here is read from a position power spectrum.
One bead is measured at a time on purpose, so tracers in the field are not the statistic.
The sample is a polystyrene bead in water under bright field; there is nothing to photodamage at these doses.
Transmitted bright field excites no dye.
This row covers the transmitted configuration, which has no spinning disk in the path.
A micrometre bead is several times larger than the diffraction-limited spot.
A micrometre bead spans many pixels at every trapping objective; the centroid is not limited by pixel sampling.
One bead near the image centre is the whole field the question needs.
Transmitted bright field has no pinhole, and one isolated bead needs no rejection of others.
The trapped bead's axial excursion is far smaller than the depth of field; the height is set by the stage, not read from focus.
One trap only: other time-shared traps would couple hydrodynamically to the measured bead.
